metadata.description: Workload name in every resource name, after the Microsoft abbreviation of its type (Cloud Adoption Framework), for example gpp-prod: ca-gpp-prod, cae-gpp-prod, kv-gpp-prod-…
Region of the regional resources. Default: the region of the resource group.
Extra tags added to every resource, for example the tags a landing zone requires.
Released image to copy into this deployment's own registry, for example <registry>.azurecr.io/com-cis-global-profile-page:1.2.3. The app then pulls it from its own registry with its managed identity.
Name of the registry token LinkCode gave for this deployment. It is used once, to copy the image during the deployment, and is not stored. Empty: the source image is public.
Password of that registry token. Used once during the deployment, not stored.
0 scales to zero when idle: cheapest, with a cold start of a few seconds on the next request.
Ignored without Redis: verification codes and token caches then live in memory, so the app runs as one replica.

Azure Managed Redis for verification codes and token caches shared by replicas. Off: one replica, in-memory caches; after a restart or scale to zero, pending codes are lost and some changes may ask the user to sign in again.
Identity provider of the users: AzureAdB2C or EntraExternalId.
Name of the identity provider tenant, for example contoso for contoso.onmicrosoft.com. Fills azureAdInstance, azureAdDomain and ropcTokenEndpoint when they are empty.
Sign-in authority host, for example https://contoso.ciamlogin.com/ or https://contoso.b2clogin.com/. Empty: derived from tenantName.
Tenant domain, for example contoso.onmicrosoft.com. Empty: derived from tenantName.
Tenant id (GUID) of the identity provider tenant used for sign-in. Empty with /setup, which finds it.

Client id of the web sign-in app registration. Empty (recommended): a tenant administrator runs /setup once after the deployment (outputs setupUrl and setupCode), which creates the registrations in the identity provider tenant and saves their settings in Key Vault.
Client id of the LinkCode setup app: a multitenant public client that /setup signs the tenant administrator in to with a device code. Keep the default.
B2C only: sign-up/sign-in user flow or custom policy. Empty for Entra External ID.
Client secret of the web sign-in app registration. Empty with /setup.
Tenant of the app registration that calls Microsoft Graph in the identity provider tenant. Empty: azureAdTenantId.
Client id of the app registration that calls Microsoft Graph. Empty: the web sign-in registration (azureAdClientId and azureAdClientSecret) also calls Graph.
Client secret of the app registration that calls Microsoft Graph. Empty when graphClientId is empty.
B2C only: token endpoint of the ROPC user flow used to check the current password. Empty: derived from tenantName and ropcPolicyId.
B2C only: name of the ROPC user flow, used with tenantName when ropcTokenEndpoint is empty.
B2C only: client id used with the ROPC user flow. Empty with /setup, which creates it.
Entra External ID with /setup: the sign-up and sign-in user flow the web registration joins. Empty: add the app to a flow in the admin center.
With /setup: the one-time code that opens it (output setupCode). A new one on every deployment; it only works while the app is not set up.
Token claim checked for step-up authentication.
Empty: step-up authentication is off.
B2C only: user flow or custom policy used for step-up authentication.
Entra External ID only: Conditional Access authentication context id used for step-up, for example c1.
Google OAuth client for account linking. Empty: linking is off.
Secret of the Google OAuth client for account linking.

Lets users add an e-mail address as a sign-in method with a one-time code, sent by Azure Communication Services (created only when on). Off: no Communication Services resources, e-mail and SMS verification are turned off, and the Security page does not offer adding these methods.

SMS sender for verification codes: a phone number bought in Azure Communication Services (E.164, for example +48123456789) or an alphanumeric sender ID enabled in ACS (1-11 letters, digits or spaces, at least one letter). Until it is set, adding a phone number is not offered.
Data location of Azure Communication Services.

Feature flag for the Recent activity page. IdentityProvider: read the tenant sign-in log through Microsoft Graph on demand (short retention). EventHub: create an event hub for the tenant Diagnostic settings and keep sign-ins in the app's own table for signInRetentionDays.
Days the app keeps sign-ins when signInActivitySource is EventHub.

Feature flag for the My Apps page: a list of the applications each user signed in to, built from the sign-in history and completed with names, logos and links from the tenant. Needs the Microsoft Graph application permission Application.Read.All on the Graph app registration.

Where the My Apps page finds the applications. TokenIssuance (default): in Azure AD B2C the audit log's "Issue an id_token to the application" events, which name the application the user signed in to (with signInActivitySource EventHub the tenant Diagnostic setting must stream AuditLogs too); Entra External ID reads its sign-in log either way. SignInLog: the sign-in history, exactly as recorded (under B2C custom policies every sign-in is ProxyIdentityExperienceFramework).

properties.scriptContent:
set -eu
for attempt in 1 2 3 4 5 6; do
  if [ -n "$SOURCE_USERNAME" ]; then
    az acr import --name "$REGISTRY" --source "$SOURCE" --image "$TARGET" --username "$SOURCE_USERNAME" --password "$SOURCE_PASSWORD" --force && exit 0
  else
    az acr import --name "$REGISTRY" --source "$SOURCE" --image "$TARGET" --force && exit 0
  fi
  echo "Import attempt $attempt failed, retrying in 30 s."
  sleep 30
done
echo "Could not copy $SOURCE into $REGISTRY. Check the registry token name and password, and that it is not expired." >&2
exit 1

metadata.description: URL of the application. Without /setup, add {appUrl}/signin-oidc as a redirect URI of the web sign-in app registration.
Without /setup: add this redirect URI to the web sign-in app registration (Authentication > Web), then sign in at appUrl.
With /setup: open this page, enter setupCode and sign in as an administrator of the identity provider tenant. Empty otherwise.
With /setup: the one-time code the setup page asks for. Empty otherwise.
Sender address of verification e-mails (Azure managed domain). Empty when enableVerificationCodes is off.
This deployment's own container registry, which holds the app's image.
Client id of the managed identity of the app.
Feature flag EventHub only: event hub authorization rule to select in the tenant's Diagnostic settings (category SignInLogs, plus AuditLogs when myAppsSource is TokenIssuance). Empty otherwise.
Feature flag EventHub only: event hub name to select in the tenant's Diagnostic settings. Empty otherwise.
